skill.name: citation-management
skill.description: Search academic sources, extract citation metadata from DOI, PMID, arXiv ID, and URLs, validate BibTeX entries, and format bibliographies for research writing.
skill.summary: Manage academic citations, metadata extraction, BibTeX validation, and bibliography formatting.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, sample URLs, placeholder API-key text, and citation-key variables. Confirmed risks are controlled but real: scripts make outbound academic API requests, can overwrite output files, and include optional Google Scholar proxy support. No prompt injection attempt or hidden obfuscated payload was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Google Scholar proxy support can route queries through unknown infrastructure.
remediation.suggestion: Remove free proxy support and do not recommend proxy rotation. Prefer official APIs, manual export, caching, and conservative rate limits.

remediation.issue: Several scripts overwrite output paths with write mode.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting, create backups, or use exclusive create mode unless the user confirms replacement.

remediation.issue: Citation identifiers and search terms are sent to external academic services.
remediation.suggestion: Document external destinations and ask before sending sensitive research topics, emails, or optional NCBI API keys.

remediation.issue: The arXiv metadata extractor uses an HTTP endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS when supported or document that arXiv identifiers may be sent over plaintext transport.

content.value_statement: Citation workflows often lose metadata, duplicate papers, and break BibTeX formatting. This skill searches sources, extracts metadata, validates references, and formats bibliographies.
actual_capabilities: Search PubMed through NCBI E-utilities and export JSON or BibTeX.
Search Google Scholar with the optional scholarly package.
Convert DOI, PMID, arXiv ID, or URL identifiers into BibTeX metadata.
Validate BibTeX required fields, DOI format, duplicate entries, and year formatting.
Format, sort, deduplicate, and clean BibTeX files.
Provide checklists and references for citation quality review.
limitations: Google Scholar search depends on the third-party scholarly package and may hit rate limits.
Some documented flags are not implemented in the bundled scripts.
Metadata accuracy depends on external databases and should be checked against source publications.
Scripts can overwrite output files when given existing paths.

output_examples.output: A search result export with PMIDs, titles, authors, journals, years, abstracts, and optional BibTeX entries.

best_practices: Review metadata against original publisher pages before final submission.
Use explicit output filenames to avoid accidental overwrites.
Respect source rate limits and avoid proxy-based scraping for large searches.
anti_patterns: Running large Google Scholar scrapes without rate limits or permission.
Accepting generated citations without checking author names, journal titles, and DOI resolution.
Overwriting the only copy of a bibliography during formatting.

faq.question: Does this work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it search PubMed?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a PubMed E-utilities script with query filters and BibTeX export.

faq.question: Can it search Google Scholar?
faq.answer: Yes, when the optional scholarly package is installed. Google Scholar rate limits can still apply.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: Most workflows do not require keys. NCBI API keys are optional and improve PubMed rate limits.

faq.question: Will it guarantee citation accuracy?
faq.answer: No. It automates checks and extraction, but users should verify important citations manually.

faq.question: Can it edit local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled scripts can write reports, BibTeX files, and formatted bibliography outputs.
